question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 11 & -9 \\ -2 & 12 & -6 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 11 & -9 \\ 0 & 23 & -15 \\ 0 & -26 & 10\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below $a_{11}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}2 & 11 & -9 \\ -2 & 12 & -6 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}+R_{1}}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 11 & -9 \\ 0 & 23 & -15 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}-2R_{1}}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 11 & -9 \\ 0 & 23 & -15 \\ 0 & -26 & 10\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{2}:=R_{2}+R_{1}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}-2R_{1}$.

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{33}=3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 5 & -12 \\ -2 & -3 & 6 \\ -8 & -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}+4R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-38 & -15 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & 6 \\ -8 & -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}-2R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-38 & -15 & 0 \\ 14 & 7 & 0 \\ -8 & -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}+4R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}-2R_{3}$.
